brief: Morgan Stanley's Savone recaps a week in which hedge funds stayed defensive despite a rally: US long/short net exposure held at 47% (5th percentile) and gross at 202% (one-year low), with the week's buying split between short covering and new longs rather than conviction adds, and roughly 40% of US L/S funds flat or down on the year. Retail (~$25bn) and resuming corporate buybacks did the actual buying. Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned, erasing about $1.7 trillion of market cap to a 13-year-low forward P/E, yet retail bought a record $1.6bn of the stock the same day institutions sold. Earnings mostly beat (CoreWeave raised, Cisco raised AI infrastructure guidance, Nebius cut guidance) and Morgan Stanley kept its $1.6 trillion 2027 hyperscaler capex forecast unchanged despite new state rules pushing about 5GW of 2028 data-center projects into 2029. A third straight hot CPI print and hawkish Fedspeak pushed December hike odds from 84% to 113% and de-rated the S&P's forward P/E from 23.2x to 18.2x. Europe diverged, with the STOXX 600 and DAX hitting records and European long/short positioning at a one-year high (90th percentile) versus the US's 5th, despite higher US yields.
